ONLY ONE OF THESE TEN ROWS IS NEW RISK. HII (rank 1) is the single genuinely new idea. Everything else is position management: two holds with levels unchanged (XLE long, XLU short) and seven exit orders to close open longs at today's open (NKE, DINO, SNX, GDX, LCII, LULU, BCC). Do not read ten rows as ten opportunities.

Research completed — the notes carry a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so truncated is false. Research ran 06:03-06:33 ET, roughly 32 minutes, well inside the cap, and captured 15 rows covering 10 distinct symbols (XLU, NKE, GDX, LCII and LULU were each re-captured once to correct evidence or conviction; the later row is published). Conviction scores were re-checked here against distinct evidence kinds and all ten match the count required (2 kinds for a 3, 3 for a 4, 4 for a 5) — four had been corrected downward during research (NKE 4 to 5 upward, GDX 4 to 3, LCII 4 to 3, LULU 4 to 3).

WHY ONE NEW IDEA AND NOT FIVE. Both of the day's live drivers were already at the three-per-driver correlation cap before research began: Iran escalation (XLE held, OXY awaiting entry, and now HII) and the long end at a 24-year high (XLU short open, plus IYR, TLT and ITB orders awaiting). DAL short — a complete, floor-clearing setup at 84.50 entry / 89.50 stop / 74.50 target, R:R 2.00, earnings 2026-10-09 bmo — was rejected on the cap rather than on merit, as were XLP short, a TLT re-level, and GD as a second defense name. Their levels are on the watchlist so a later run can lift them if a slot frees up. The third driver found, AI and IT-services demand verified through Accenture's record print, failed on its own expressions: SNX's catalyst is spent with $15.7M of insider selling and zero buys, EPAM is mechanically contradicted (headcount-based engineering is what GenAI disintermediates), and MU has tripled in six months on a now-spent print.

SEVEN EXITS IN ONE MORNING IS THE UNUSUAL NUMBER HERE, and the reason is one rule applied consistently rather than seven separate thesis failures. Five of the seven (NKE, BCC, LCII, LULU, plus the structure problem on DINO and SNX) are positions carrying no stop at all or no stop that can be set compliantly from a filled entry that cannot be amended. NKE is the only one closed on fresh fundamental news — its Q1 FY27 release guided FY27 revenue down high-single-digits. DINO and SNX are closed in profit (+4.8% and +4.5%) precisely because their arithmetic no longer closes from the filled entry: DINO needs a 129.50 target above its two-year high to clear 2.0 R:R on a compliant 2.0-ATR stop, and SNX yields only 1.30 R:R from 260.00 with a 2.0-ATR stop. Taking the profit beats keeping a stop walked in to 1.83 ATR, which is the failure mode that produced all ten of this report's first stop-outs.

RATIOS SITTING JUST ABOVE THE FLOOR — read this honestly. Both holds clear the 2.0 swing floor narrowly: XLE at 2.13 and XLU at 2.07. That clustering is normally the signature of targets fitted to pass, and it is called out rather than hidden. The mitigating fact is that neither level was set today: both are the entry, target and stop as first published (XLE 2026-08-15, XLU 2026-09-24) and neither stop has been walked in — XLE's is 2.37 ATR from entry on a fetched ATR14 of 1.3062 and XLU's is 2.35 ATR on 0.5736, both above the 1.8 ATR ETF floor. HII is the only freshly set ratio and it is 2.79 on a 2.78-ATR stop. All three recomputed here from entry, target and stop rather than carried from the notes.

PRICES. Every price in this report is the 2026-10-01 regular-session close, fetched from finnhub at 20:00Z and re-fetched at synthesis; the market session at synthesis is pre-market, so a previous close is the freshest honest equity mark, not stale data. Index, VIX, futures, dollar, crude, Brent and gold levels in market_context could NOT be fetched from a market-data call — Yahoo's chart API returned HTTP 429 for every index, futures, FX and commodity symbol tried and finnhub refuses indices — so those numbers come from fetched news articles (investrade.com market review and CNBC oil coverage, both cited) rather than from a quote. VIX and DXY could not be obtained from any source and are null. Bitcoin at $86,344 is a fetched CoinGecko price.

OTHER GAPS THAT COST SOMETHING. (1) Event contracts: none publishable. Kalshi's unauthenticated endpoint returns markets as active with null bid, ask, last and volume, and market_data.py events returns count 0 for every macro topic tried, so no implied probability could be fetched and a probability-disagreement thesis is impossible this run. (2) Earnings calendar hole 2026-10-17 to 2026-11-02: --days 12 covers Oct 2-16 and --days 40 returns only Nov 3-11, so there is no fetched earnings date for HII, GD, LMT, NOC, RTX, PFE, CCJ or KHC. (5) No crude futures idea (/MCL) despite the universe file preferring futures for a commodity view, because no futures price or contract-month data could be fetched. (6) No long_term idea published. The lane was worked deliberately — P&C insurers (TRV, CB, WRB, ACGL) as beneficiaries of a permanently higher long end — and rejected for two reasons, one of them a gap in the work: the group's de-rating has a real cause the thesis did not address (TRV's sell-side is cutting through an 83% beat, pricing the underwriting cycle softening), and no bear-case price could be built without book value per share and normalised ROE, neither of which was available from any source here. RED TEAM (phase 2c). Ten recommendations in, two out. Cut HII, the day's single new idea and its only conviction 5: the catalyst it is keyed to — a carrier strike group deploying — is an operations decision that adds no revenue to a shipbuilder with a 4.2x-revenue backlog, and the idea's own CR evidence freezes the procurement channel until 2026-12-11, past the horizon. THE SEVEN EXITS ARE ENDORSED ON SUBSTANCE AND MOVED TO THE WATCHLIST ON MECHANICS, and the distinction matters: closing NKE, DINO, SNX, GDX, LCII, LULU and BCC is right — five of the seven carry no stop at all and three sit within 1% of a 120-day low. But this report has no way to say 'close a position'. publish_sheets.positions_from_report turns every recommendation into a new PENDING row keyed on (symbol, direction), so a direction=sell exit order does not close the long; it opens a phantom short. This has already shipped twice: the 2026-09-08 NKE and LULU 'sell' rows are both carried today as open, filled shorts being marked to market at +7.81% and +4.39%, while the NKE and LULU longs they were meant to close remain open at -11.5% and -16.4%. The GLD 406.77 row is the third, and yesterday's watchlist misread it as a stale order rather than an artifact; that entry is corrected here. Publishing seven more would have added five phantom shorts and amended two, and all seven would have been demoted by --enforce regardless (no entry, no target, no stop), under a generated note that loses the instruction. On the watchlist the instruction survives in full and the tracker stays clean. Two caveats the reader must not miss: the tab heads these rows 'WATCHLIST — not yet actionable', which is the opposite of what they say, so read the notes; and nothing in the pipeline closes a position, so each long must be marked closed in state/open_positions.json by hand. The real fix is a close/exit direction the publisher understands, which is a code change and outside this phase.

EXPECT XLE TO BE DEMOTED AT 2d. Its catalyst is stamped 2026-10-01, so check_catalyst_date fails it as already passed. That is the right rule for a new entry and the wrong reading of a hold on a position filled 2026-09-16, whose dated support is the carrier arrival at end of November. If XLE lands in the watchlist, the position is unaffected: it stays open and graded in the Performance tab either way.

WHAT SURVIVES IS TWO HOLDS AND NO NEW RISK. Both say hold at unchanged levels and explicitly say do not add, so the actionable content of this morning is seven closes and nothing bought. market_context.summary: Bear steepener plus an oil shock, and that combination is what sorts today's book. The 10-year closed 5.248% on 2026-10-01 after spiking to roughly 5.34% intraday, a new 24-year high, with effective fed funds at 3.88% and the 2-year at 4.88% — funds well below the 2-year says this is a term-premium problem and a market pricing the path up rather than a tightening cycle. Equities clawed back to close slightly green (S&P 500 7,666 +0.20%, Nasdaq 26,871 +0.04%, Russell 2000 2,806 +0.35%) with tech, semis, software, industrials and energy leading while homebuilders, mortgage lenders, banks and REITs lagged — REITs are down about 9% since late August on this one axis. Separately, Brent broke $100 to $102.31 (+4.4%) and WTI to $92.87 after the WSJ reported a third US carrier strike group ordered to the Middle East, the USS Theodore Roosevelt arriving end of November; this is a war premium, not a demand story, and oil already touched $108 on 2026-09-10, so $102 is mid-range in an active conflict rather than a top. Gold set a fresh high at $4,203.30. The actionable asymmetry today is a cross-asset divergence: the oil market repriced Iran escalation and defense equities, de-rated all year on an interim US-Iran peace agreement, did not — which is the one new idea on the page. The day's dated event is the September Employment Situation at 08:30 ET, consensus +84k with unemployment held at 4.1%.

If that is the dominant driver then 16% of de-rating is the opportunity rather than the trend. Against it, the de-rating has run six weeks in step with the long end rather than with any change in load-growth news, and REITs are down about 9% on the same axis over the same window.
